title: The base field is relatively algebraically closed in a finite purely transcendental extension
statement: Let $L/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose that for a finite integer $r\geq 0$ there is a $k$-isomorphism $L\cong k(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$, where $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ are algebraically independent over $k$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree] and the right hand side is the fraction field of $k[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$; thus $L/k$ is purely transcendental [def-trf-purely-transcendental-extension]. Then $k$ is algebraically closed in $L$: for every $\alpha\in L$ satisfying a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in $k$, there exists $a\in k$ whose image under the structure embedding $k\hookrightarrow L$ is $\alpha$. This includes $r=0$, when $L\cong k$.

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof paragraph beginning 'Let $T$ be the connected component': the field-theoretic input implicit in applying the connected-point criterion to the purely transcendental residue field. The coprime-polynomial argument is retained in report.md for the future worker.

proof.text: Choose the given k-algebra equivalence e from L to F = Frac(A), with A = k[U_1,...,U_r] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The image x = e(alpha) is integral over k: over a field, algebraicity implies integrality (Mathlib IsAlgebraic.isIntegral), and integral relations are preserved by algebra homomorphisms. The scalar assertion transports back by injectivity and the scalar-commutation equation of e.

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, implicit constant-field input in the connected-component paragraph; implemented with Mathlib integral-element API.

proof.text: Prove A is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] by induction on r. For r = 0, MvPolynomial.isEmptyRingEquiv identifies A with k. For r+1, MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv identifies A with the one-variable polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring] over the r-variable ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain] to the induction hypothesis and transport integral closedness through this ring equivalence (IsIntegrallyClosed.of_equiv). Domains are supplied by the polynomial-ring instances.

source.place: Tag 030A, lemma-polynomial-domain-normal; finite induction implemented using MvPolynomial.isEmptyRingEquiv and MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv.

proof.text: The monic relation for x over k is also a monic relation over A, by mapping its coefficients along k to A (IsIntegral.tower_top). Integral closedness [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] therefore gives p in A with image x in F. Since A to F is injective, the same monic relation implies p is integral over k (isIntegral_algebraMap_iff). If p = 0, alpha is the image of zero.

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, implicit constant-field input in the connected-component paragraph; implemented with Mathlib integral-element API.

proof.text: If p is nonzero, the Mathlib theorem IsIntegral.isUnit makes p a unit of A: a nonzero element integral over a field is invertible in the domain containing it. Thus p divides 1 = C(1). Apply [lem-trf-mvpolynomial-divisor-nonzero-constant] with a = 1 to obtain p = C(b) for some b in k. The scalar-tower identity gives x = algebraMap(k,F)(b), and the k-algebra equivalence transports this equality to alpha = algebraMap(k,L)(b). This uses the existing divisor lemma with the simpler nonzero constant 1 rather than extracting a constant term explicitly.

Stacks 057K (more-morphisms.tex l.13432 ff.) uses this field fact without proving it, so proof_origin by agent is right. Step 1 is an elementary reduction to Frac(k[U_1..U_r]); algebraic independence is the same as injective evaluation, and the r=0 and α=0 cases are handled. Step 2 proves normality of the polynomial ring by an explicit induction using the one-variable Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain (Stacks 030A), plus the monomial-grouping isomorphism. Step 3 is elementary: a monic relation with c_0≠0, n≥1, and normality give h∈A over α. Step 4 gets h∣C(c_0) from injectivity of A→F and then applies the new leaf to get h=C(b). The new leaf is an exact match for MvPolynomial.dvd_C_iff_exists (NoZeroDivisors.lean:93, variables CommSemiring+NoZeroDivisors at l.33/39, a≠0). It is self-contained and statement-only. I tested it on J=∅, a=0 (excluded), ℤ/4 (1+2X, showing the domain hypothesis is needed) and ℤ.
